While only isolated showers are visible on satellite this afternoon,
the Marianas sits along a convergence zone between TD Jangmi and the
easterly trade winds. With the addition of plenty of moisture and 
upper level instability, this is expected to allow for the 
development of scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms tonight 
through at least tomorrow while Jangmi remains nearby. Precipitation 
chances will begin decreasing Friday night as Jangmi moves away and 
the convergence zone drifts off to the west. A dryer, weak trade wind
flow is expected to take it's place and will bring isolated showers 
for the rest of the forecast period.

Marine... Seas are expected to become elevated and potentially 
reaching near hazardous criteria for small craft tonight for the next
several days as opposing swell directions bring peaky seas. Combined
seas will build to 6 to 8 feet tonight as southwest swell from 
Jangmi moves into the Marianas. This combined with the ongoing trade 
swell and lingering northwest swell will bring a moderate risk of rip
currents to all reefs. Moderate southeasterly winds will diminish 
back down to light to moderate starting Thursday. After peaking 
tonight or tomorrow, seas will slowly decrease down to 4 to 6 feet by
the weekend.

Tropical Systems...
At 1 PM, Tropical Depression Jangmi (06W) was centered about 295
miles north-northwest of Yap Proper near 13.1N 135.7E, moving
northwest at 15 mph. Jangmi is expected to continue to move
northwest, slowing down a bit as it moves farther away from Yap 
Proper and Palau. Jangmi is not expected to directly affect any 
islands within the Guam Area of Responsibility. The latest forecast 
has Jangmi strengthening over the next couple of days, possibly 
becoming a tropical storm this evening, and a typhoon Friday night or
Saturday. The current track takes Jangmi toward the southern islands
of Japan, including Okinawa.

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and from the
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Partly cloudy skies with isolated showers are seen across Pohnpei 
and Kosrae this afternoon, while mostly cloudy skies with scattered
showers are seen over Majuro. Altimetry shows seas between 4 and 5
feet for Kosrae and Pohnpei, with seas of 5 to 7 feet seen east of
Majuro.

A fairly dry pattern is currently seen over Pohnpei and Kosrae,
though increasing convection is seen to the north and east of both
islands. Isolated showers are expected to increase by Friday morning
along a northwest to southeast oriented surface trough just north of
the islands that is expected to drift west over the coming days. This
feature looks to bring increased POPs (Probability of Precipitation)
to the region for the next couple of days. Farther east, a developing
Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) was seen to the east of Majuro
this morning. However, an advancing weak trade-wind trough is helping
the convergence associated with the ITCZ to spread west over the
Marshalls, bringing increased POPs to Majuro this afternoon. As the
ITCZ continues to strengthen and weak trade-wind troughs move across
the region, expect increased showers and thunderstorms to continue 
across majuro, with numerous showers expected Friday and Friday 
night. As the ITCZ slowly spreads west, interactions with the ITCZ 
and trade-wind troughs will maintain an overall wet pattern across 
the Marshall Islands, then into Kosrae and Pohnpei late in the 
weekend into next week. A drier trade-wind pattern then looks to 
develop across Kosrae and Pohnpei early next week. 

For the marine forecast, relatively benign conditions are expected 
to continue through the weekend. For Pohnpei and Kosrae, light to
gentle winds look to continue into next week, with combined seas of 3
to 5 feet subsiding to between 2 and 4 feet. For Majuro, gentle to 
moderate winds will slowly decrease, becoming light to gentle by 
Saturday morning, and remaining light to gentle into next week. 
Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet will slowly subside to between 3 and 5 
feet over the weekend.

Western Micronesia...
Tropical depression 06W (Jangmi) continues to move further away from
Yap Proper and Palau. However the monsoon tail is firmly over both
islands. This tail is bringing high-end scattered showers and
isolated thunderstorms. Once Jangmi detaches from the monsoon trough,
the trough is expected to reorient itself back over Palau and Yap.
This will keep showers in the forecast for these islands through at 
least the middle of next week. 

Over in Chuuk, a trade-wind regime is starting set up over the
region. A few troughs bringing a few off and on showers. However,
